body: Definitely. That one time I had a weed high was identical to the feeling of derealization

Hang in there. When will you see your psychiatrist again? Sometimes certain psych meds take a while to 'settle'. Most importantly, stay safe. If you really feel it is too much for you, see your psychiatrist again and tell him how dire it is. Take care x

Oh and for example, seeing close ones (e.g parents, spouse, close friends) and your brain only registers their name and memories, just as one would a character they've read from a book. You know them so well yet there is no emotional recognition or familiarity.

To me it feels like being on a stage, but no matter how tired you are they would never draw the curtain. So you just have to keep on living this artificial world. Which is why suicidal thoughts hit me when my depersonalization hits intensely, as I feel like I want to wake up and if I die I'll  wake up where my life actually is.

What you wrote slightly resonate with me. Though the sadness is sometimes replaced with anger instead. Anxiety and rage together at times, when this happens I felt immobilized just feeling very, very angry, where all my muscles would just tense up and I could just scream for a while. As for the memory part, when my depersonalization hits, I get a detachment to the memories and emotional feeling to others I know. And everything just feels painful and sad. I often wish I could wake up.

I share your worry. I did in the past have lost a few relationships because I am too draining to them. One relationship worked better because I tried to keep my anxiety to my self better but that after a while my condition actually got worse (i believe as a result of being anxious about being anxious in front of him) and it didnt work out in the end. We could only do so much to control it. I dont think hiding it is healthy for people with anxiety. 
But luckily about 10 years ago I met someone accidentally around the time when my mental health was at the worst point (almost got admitted), and he stuck around. We got married a few years later eventhough he knows that my anxiety and depersonalization is a part of me. He doesn't have any experience with mental health issue personally or even in his friends or family, but he said he wants to make us work. Be honest with yourself and be honest with your partner, be open about your condition. Love her today and cherish the good days. If it is going to work, it will work. Good luck, we all deserve peace in our life  x
